method.public_headline: POB novelty × square-root(reference consensus); documented risk is excluded

pob.text: The word of Yahweh that came to Joel son of Pethuel[a][b].

spob.text: Yahweh’s word came to Joel son of Pethuel.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel:
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh’s word that came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
public_domain_references.asv: The word of Jehovah that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.
public_domain_references.kjv: The word of the LORD that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.
public_domain_references.brenton: The word of the Lord which came to Joel the son of Bathuel.

pob.text: Hear this[a], you elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land: Has this happened in your days[b], or in the days of your fathers?

spob.text: Listen to this, you elders. Pay attention, all who live in the land.[a] Has this happened in your lifetime or in the time of your fathers?[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Hear this, O elders; and give ear, all who dwell in the land. Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
public_domain_references.web: Hear this, you elders, and listen, all you inhabitants of the land! Has this ever happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
public_domain_references.asv: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land. Hath this been in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
public_domain_references.kjv: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land. Hath this been in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?
public_domain_references.brenton: Hear these [words], ye elders, and hearken all ye that inhabit the land. Have such things happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?

pob.text: Tell your children about it[a], and let your children tell their children, and their children tell another generation.

spob.text: Tell your children about it. Let them tell their children, and let their children tell another generation.

public_domain_references.bsb: Tell it to your children; let your children tell it to their children, and their children to the next generation.
public_domain_references.web: Tell your children about it, and have your children tell their children, and their children, another generation.
public_domain_references.asv: Tell ye your children of it, and [let] your children [tell] their children, and their children another generation.
public_domain_references.kjv: Tell ye your children of it, and [let] your children [tell] their children, and their children another generation.
public_domain_references.brenton: Tell your children concerning them, and [let] your children [tell] their children, and their children another generation.

pob.text: What the cutting locust left[a], the swarming locust ate; and what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust ate; and what the hopping locust left, the devouring locust ate.

spob.text: The swarming locusts ate what the cutting locusts had left. The hopping locusts ate what the swarming locusts had left. Then the devouring locusts ate what the hopping locusts had left.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust has left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust has left, the destroying locust has eaten.
public_domain_references.web: What the swarming locust has left, the great locust has eaten. What the great locust has left, the grasshopper has eaten. What the grasshopper has left, the caterpillar has eaten.
public_domain_references.asv: That which the palmer-worm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the canker-worm eaten; and that which the canker-worm hath left hath the caterpillar eaten.
public_domain_references.kjv: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
public_domain_references.brenton: The leavings of the caterpillar has the locust eaten, and the leavings of the locust has the palmerworm eaten, and the leavings of the palmerworm has the cankerworm eaten.

pob.text: Wake up[a], you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, over the sweet wine, because it has been cut off from your mouth.

spob.text: Wake up, you drunkards! Weep and wail, all you who drink wine, because the sweet wine[a] has been cut off from your mouths.

public_domain_references.bsb: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.
public_domain_references.web: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
public_domain_references.asv: Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and wail, all ye drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine; for it is cut off from your mouth.
public_domain_references.kjv: Awake, ye drunkards, and weep; and howl, all ye drinkers of wine, because of the new wine; for it is cut off from your mouth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Awake, ye drunkards, from your wine, and weep: mourn, all ye that drink wine to drunkenness: for joy and gladness are removed from your mouth.

pob.text: For a nation has come up against my land[a], mighty and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion[b], and it has the fangs of a lioness.

spob.text: For a nation has invaded my land.[a] It is powerful and beyond counting. Its teeth are like a lion’s teeth, and its fangs are like a lioness’s fangs.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: For a nation has invaded My land, powerful and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its fangs are the fangs of a lioness.
public_domain_references.web: For a nation has come up on my land, strong, and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the fangs of a lioness.
public_domain_references.asv: For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number; his teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he hath the jaw-teeth of a lioness.
public_domain_references.kjv: For a nation is come up upon my land, strong, and without number, whose teeth [are] the teeth of a lion, and he hath the cheek teeth of a great lion.
public_domain_references.brenton: For a strong and innumerable nation is come up against my land, their teeth are lion's teeth, and their back teeth those of a [lion's] whelp.

pob.text: It has made my vine a desolation and my fig tree splinters[a]; it has stripped it bare and thrown it down[b]; its branches have turned white.

spob.text: It has devastated my vine and reduced my fig tree to splinters.[a] It has stripped the tree bare and thrown it down. Its bare branches have turned white.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white.
public_domain_references.web: He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
public_domain_references.asv: He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig-tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white.
public_domain_references.kjv: He hath laid my vine waste, and barked my fig tree: he hath made it clean bare, and cast [it] away; the branches thereof are made white.
public_domain_references.brenton: He has ruined my vine, and utterly broken my fig-trees: he has utterly searched [my vine], and cast it down; he has peeled its branches.

pob.text: Wail like a virgin clothed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth[a][b].

spob.text: Wail like a virgin wearing rough sackcloth in mourning for the husband of her youth.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.
public_domain_references.web: Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth!
public_domain_references.asv: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Lament to me more than a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.

pob.text: The grain offering and the drink offering are cut off from the house of Yahweh[a]; the priests mourn[c][b], the ministers of Yahweh.

spob.text: Grain offerings and drink offerings have ceased at Yahweh’s house—the temple. The priests who serve Yahweh mourn.

public_domain_references.bsb: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: The meal offering and the drink offering are cut off from Yahweh’s house. The priests, Yahweh’s ministers, mourn.
public_domain_references.asv: The meal-offering and the drink-offering are cut off from the house of Jehovah; the priests, Jehovah’s ministers, mourn.
public_domain_references.kjv: The meat offering and the drink offering is cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the LORD’s ministers, mourn.
public_domain_references.brenton: The meat-offering and drink-offering are removed from the house of the Lord: mourn, ye priests that serve at the altar of the Lord.

pob.text: The field is devastated; the ground mourns[a], for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, the oil has failed.

spob.text: The fields are ruined, and the ground mourns, because the grain crop is destroyed, the new wine has dried up, and the olive oil supply[a] has failed.

public_domain_references.bsb: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.
public_domain_references.web: The field is laid waste. The land mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
public_domain_references.asv: The field is laid waste, the land mourneth; for the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth.
public_domain_references.kjv: The field is wasted, the land mourneth; for the corn is wasted: the new wine is dried up, the oil languisheth.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the plains languish: let the land mourn, for the corn languishes; the wine is dried up, the oil becomes scarce;

pob.text: Be ashamed[a], farmers; wail, vinedressers, over the wheat and over the barley[b], because the harvest of the field has perished.

spob.text: Farmers, be ashamed![a] Vineyard workers, wail[b] over the wheat and barley, because the field’s harvest is ruined.

public_domain_references.bsb: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
public_domain_references.web: Be confounded, you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field has perished.
public_domain_references.asv: Be confounded, O ye husbandmen, wail, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the field is perished.
public_domain_references.kjv: Be ye ashamed, O ye husbandmen; howl, O ye vinedressers, for the wheat and for the barley; because the harvest of the field is perished.
public_domain_references.brenton: the husbandmen are consumed: mourn your property on account of the wheat and barley; for the harvest has perished from off the field.

pob.text: The vine has dried up[a], and the fig tree has withered; the pomegranate, also the palm and the apple tree—all the trees of the field have dried up. Indeed[b], joy has dried up from the sons of man.

spob.text: The grapevine has dried up, and the fig tree has withered. The pomegranate, the palm, and the apple tree[a] have also dried up. Every tree in the fields has dried up. Indeed, joy has dried up from the sons of man.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard—are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.
public_domain_references.web: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered— the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the trees of the field are withered; for joy has withered away from the sons of men.
public_domain_references.asv: The vine is withered, and the fig-tree languisheth; the pomegranate-tree, the palm-tree also, and the apple-tree, even all the trees of the field are withered: for joy is withered away from the sons of men.
public_domain_references.kjv: The vine is dried up, and the fig tree languisheth; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, [even] all the trees of the field, are withered: because joy is withered away from the sons of men.
public_domain_references.brenton: The vine is dried up, and the fig-trees are become few; the pomegranate, and palm-tree, and apple, and all the trees of the field are dried up: for the sons of men have abolished joy.

pob.text: Gird yourselves and mourn[a], O priests; wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God[b], because grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.

spob.text: Priests, put on sackcloth and mourn. Wail, you who serve at the altar. Come and spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God, because grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.
public_domain_references.web: Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! Wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, lie all night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for the meal offering and the drink offering are withheld from your God’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: Gird yourselves [with sackcloth], and lament, ye priests; wail, ye ministers of the altar; come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meal-offering and the drink-offering are withholden from the house of your God.
public_domain_references.kjv: Gird yourselves, and lament, ye priests: howl, ye ministers of the altar: come, lie all night in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: for the meat offering and the drink offering is withholden from the house of your God.
public_domain_references.brenton: Gird yourselves [with sackcloth], and lament, ye priests: mourn, ye that serve at the altar: go in, sleep in sackcloths, ye that minister to God: for the meat-offering and drink-offering are withheld from the house of your God.

pob.text: Consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders[a], all the inhabitants of the land, to the house of Yahweh your God, and cry out to Yahweh.

spob.text: Set apart a sacred time for fasting. Call a solemn assembly. Bring the elders and everyone who lives in the land[a] to the house of Yahweh your God, and cry out to Yahweh.

public_domain_references.bsb: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: Sanctify a fast. Call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land to the house of Yahweh, your God, and cry to Yahweh.
public_domain_references.asv: Sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the old men [and] all the inhabitants of the land unto the house of Jehovah your God, and cry unto Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders [and] all the inhabitants of the land [into] the house of the LORD your God, and cry unto the LORD,
public_domain_references.brenton: Sanctify a fast, proclaim a [solemn] service, gather the elders [and] all the inhabitants of the land into the house of your God, and cry earnestly to the Lord,

pob.text: Alas for the day! For the day of Yahweh is near[a], and it comes like destruction from the Almighty.

spob.text: How terrible that day will be! The day of Yahweh is near. It is coming like destruction from the Almighty.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Alas for the day! For the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
public_domain_references.web: Alas for the day! For the day of Yahweh is at hand, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
public_domain_references.asv: Alas for the day! for the day of Jehovah is at hand, and as destruction from the Almighty shall it come.
public_domain_references.kjv: Alas for the day! for the day of the LORD [is] at hand, and as a destruction from the Almighty shall it come.
public_domain_references.brenton: Alas, alas, alas for the day! for the day of the Lord is nigh, and it will come as trouble upon trouble.

pob.text: Is not food cut off before our eyes[b][a], joy and gladness from the house of our God?

spob.text: Hasn't food been cut off before our very eyes? Haven't joy and gladness also been cut off from the house of our God?[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes— joy and gladness from the house of our God?
public_domain_references.web: Isn’t the food cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
public_domain_references.asv: Is not the food cut off before our eyes, [yea], joy and gladness from the house of our God?
public_domain_references.kjv: Is not the meat cut off before our eyes, [yea], joy and gladness from the house of our God?
public_domain_references.brenton: [Your] meat has been destroyed before your eyes, joy and gladness from out of the house of your God.

pob.text: The seeds have shriveled beneath their clods[a]; the storehouses are desolate, the granaries are torn down[b], because the grain has dried up.

spob.text: The seeds[a] have shriveled under the clumps of soil.[b] The storehouses stand in ruins, and the granaries have been torn down, because the grain has dried up.

public_domain_references.bsb: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.
public_domain_references.web: The seeds rot under their clods. The granaries are laid desolate. The barns are broken down, for the grain has withered.
public_domain_references.asv: The seeds rot under their clods; the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the grain is withered.
public_domain_references.kjv: The seed is rotten under their clods, the garners are laid desolate, the barns are broken down; for the corn is withered.
public_domain_references.brenton: The heifers have started at their mangers, the treasures are abolished, the wine-presses are broken down; for the corn is withered.

pob.text: How the animals groan! The herds of cattle wander in confusion[a], because there is no pasture for them[b]; even the flocks of sheep suffer.

spob.text: The animals groan! The cattle herds wander in confusion because they have nowhere to graze. Even the flocks of sheep suffer.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
public_domain_references.web: How the animals groan! The herds of livestock are perplexed, because they have no pasture. Yes, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
public_domain_references.asv: How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
public_domain_references.kjv: How do the beasts groan! the herds of cattle are perplexed, because they have no pasture; yea, the flocks of sheep are made desolate.
public_domain_references.brenton: What shall we store up for ourselves? the herds of cattle have mourned, because they had no pasture; and the flocks of sheep have been utterly destroyed.

pob.text: To you[a], O Yahweh, I call, for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness[c][b], and flame has scorched all the trees of the field.

spob.text: Yahweh, I cry out to you, because fire has devoured the wilderness pastures, and flame has scorched every tree in the field.

public_domain_references.bsb: To You, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh, I cry to you, for the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame has burned all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.asv: O Jehovah, to thee do I cry; for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.kjv: O LORD, to thee will I cry: for the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and the flame hath burned all the trees of the field.
public_domain_references.brenton: To thee, O Lord, will I cry: for fire has devoured the fair places of the wilderness, and a flame has burnt up all the trees of the field.

pob.text: Even the beasts of the field pant for you[a], because the channels of water have dried up[c][b], and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.

spob.text: Even the animals in the fields pant for you,[a] because the streams have dried up and fire has burned up the grazing lands in the wilderness.

public_domain_references.bsb: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.
public_domain_references.web: Yes, the animals of the field pant to you, for the water brooks have dried up, and the fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, the beasts of the field pant unto thee; for the water brooks are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
public_domain_references.kjv: The beasts of the field cry also unto thee: for the rivers of waters are dried up, and the fire hath devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the cattle of the field have looked up to thee: for the fountains of waters have been dried up, and fire has devoured the fair places of the wilderness.

pob.text: Blow a horn in Zion[a], and sound an alarm on my holy mountain; let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Yahweh is coming—indeed, it is near.

spob.text: Blow a horn in Zion! Sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let everyone who lives in the land[a] tremble, because the day of Yahweh is coming. It is near.

public_domain_references.bsb: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—
public_domain_references.web: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Yahweh comes, for it is close at hand:
public_domain_references.asv: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain; let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of Jehovah cometh, for it is nigh at hand;
public_domain_references.kjv: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the LORD cometh, for [it is] nigh at hand;
public_domain_references.brenton: Sound the trumpet in Sion, make a proclamation in my holy mountain, and let all the inhabitants of the land be confounded: for the day of the Lord is near;

pob.text: A day of darkness and gloom[a], a day of clouds and thick darkness; like dawn spread over the mountains, a great and mighty people comes. Nothing like it has ever been from of old, and after it there will not again be any[c][b], through the years of generation after generation.

spob.text: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like dawn spreading over the mountains,[a] a great and mighty people[b] is coming. Nothing like it has ever appeared since ancient times, and nothing like it will come again through generation after generation.

public_domain_references.bsb: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness. Like the dawn overspreading the mountains a great and strong army appears, such as never was of old, nor will ever be in ages to come.
public_domain_references.web: A day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. As the dawn spreading on the mountains, a great and strong people; there has never been the like, neither will there be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.
public_domain_references.asv: a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, as the dawn spread upon the mountains; a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after them, even to the years of many generations.
public_domain_references.kjv: A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, [even] to the years of many generations.
public_domain_references.brenton: for a day of darkness and gloominess is near, a day of cloud and mist: a numerous and strong people shall be spread upon the mountains as the morning; there has not been from the beginning one like it, and after it there shall not be again even to the years of many generations.

pob.text: Before it[a], fire devours; behind it, a flame blazes. The land before it is like the garden of Eden, but behind it is a desolate wilderness; indeed, nothing escapes it.

spob.text: As it advances, fire devours what lies ahead, and flames blaze behind it. The land before it is like the garden of Eden, but the land it leaves behind becomes a desolate wilderness. Nothing escapes it.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland— surely nothing will escape them.
public_domain_references.web: A fire devours before them, and behind them, a flame burns. The land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them, a desolate wilderness. Yes, and no one has escaped them.
public_domain_references.asv: A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and none hath escaped them.
public_domain_references.kjv: A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land [is] as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them.
public_domain_references.brenton: Before them is a consuming fire, and behind them is a flame kindled: the land before them is as a paradise of delight, and behind them a desolate plain: and there shall none of them escape.

pob.text: Their appearance is like the appearance of horses[a], and like horsemen[b], so they run.

spob.text: They[a] look like horses, and they run like horsemen.

public_domain_references.bsb: Their appearance is like that of horses, and they gallop like swift steeds.
public_domain_references.web: Their appearance is as the appearance of horses, and they run as horsemen.
public_domain_references.asv: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so do they run.
public_domain_references.kjv: The appearance of them [is] as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run.
public_domain_references.brenton: Their appearance is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they pursue.

pob.text: Like the sound of chariots[a], they leap on the tops of the mountains; like the sound of a flame of fire consuming stubble[c][b]; like a mighty people arrayed for battle.

spob.text: They leap across the mountaintops with a sound like chariots. Their noise is like a flame consuming the dry stalks left in a field. They are like a mighty people lined up for battle.

public_domain_references.bsb: With a sound like that of chariots they bound over the mountaintops, like the crackling of fire consuming stubble, like a mighty army deployed for battle.
